goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection/breakage in migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:28 — old site setting host values are string-interpolated into the INSERT instead of being quoted or parameterized

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The `h` value comes from the `site_settings` table (previous `embeddable_hosts` setting) and is inserted without escaping/quoting beyond surrounding single quotes. If `h` contains a `'` (or other SQL metacharacters), the INSERT can break or be exploited as SQL injection during migration. Even if the UI intended `host_list`, the DB value isn’t guaranteed safe here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 uses create_table force: true, silently dropping and recreating an existing table and losing data on re-run

adjudication.rationale: The migration explicitly calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which (in Rails) will drop the table if it already exists and recreate it. That does indeed make the migration non-idempotent and can cause silent data loss if the migration is re-run on a DB where `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., after a failed/partial run or manual re-execution). This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_host.rb:2 has no uniqueness validation or DB index on host, allowing duplicate rows for the same host

adjudication.rationale: In the new `EmbeddableHost` model (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`) there is only a `validates_format_of :host` and no `validates_uniqueness_of :host` (case-insensitive or otherwise). The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table without any unique index/constraint on `host`. Therefore, the code as introduced allows multiple rows with the same host value to be created (via the admin controller create/update or via the migration import), which is a verifiable data-integrity issue for an “allowed hosts” list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 update action performs no writes, so the client's saveChanges silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not persist anything; it simply re-renders the serialized embedding object (same as `#show`). However, the client-side `saveChanges` action (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`) is not wired up in the provided template (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs` has no button/action invoking `saveChanges`), and the actual “saving” behavior for hosts is implemented via `EmbeddableHost` create/update/destroy calls. So while `#update` is a no-op, the diff does not verifiably show a user-visible save operation that is broken or “silently does nothing.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Format validation in embeddable_host.rb:1 permits a :port suffix, but record_for_host matches against uri.host without a port, so hosts stored with ports can never be allowed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` validation allows an optional `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` port suffix in `host`, and `before_validation` strips scheme and paths but does not strip ports, so a stored value like `example.com:3000` is possible. However, `record_for_host` parses the referer via `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`; `uri.host` excludes the port (Ruby URI stores it in `uri.port`). Therefore entries saved with ports will never match and `host_allowed?` will incorrectly deny them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_id in the embeddable_hosts migration is null: false with no foreign key or dependent: handling; deleting a category leaves orphaned hosts and TopicEmbed.import creates posts in a dead category

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts.category_id` as `null: false` but adds no foreign key constraint, and the model `EmbeddableHost` only has `belongs_to :category` with no dependent behavior or validation to prevent dangling references. If a Category is deleted, existing `embeddable_hosts` rows will keep a now-invalid `category_id` (orphaned host records). Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` now sets `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (an id) based on the `EmbeddableHost` record; if that `category_id` no longer corresponds to an existing category, the embed import path can attempt to create posts targeting a non-existent category (behavior then depends on PostCreator, but the invalid reference is clearly possible from this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6:196 — obj[k].map(...) can produce null entries when sub-type lookup fails and `hydrated || []` is dead code, leaking nulls into the hydrated collection

adjudication.rationale: In store.js.es6 `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural-IDs branch does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(function(id) { return self._lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root); });` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead code when `obj[k]` is an array. More importantly, if `_lookupSubType` returns `null`/`undefined` for any missing ID, those values will be present in the resulting array and get assigned into the hydrated collection without filtering, which can propagate invalid entries to callers expecting objects.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6:192 — the _ids branch assumes obj[k] is an array; a scalar or null attribute ending in _ids throws on .map

adjudication.rationale: In discourse/models/store.js.es6, _hydrateEmbedded was extended to match keys ending in `_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. In the plural (`m[2]` truthy) branch it immediately does `obj[k].map(...)` with no guard. If the server payload includes a `_ids` key whose value is `null`, a scalar, or otherwise not an array, this will throw `TypeError: obj[k].map is not a function` at runtime. This is a concrete correctness/robustness issue introduced by the diff (previous code only handled singular `_id` values).

adjudication_records.issue_text: adapters/rest.js.es6:22 — type.replace('_', '-') lacks the /g flag, so multi-underscore admin model names don't resolve to the /admin/ base path

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `ADMIN_MODELS` contains only `'plugin'`, `'site-customization'`, and `'embeddable-host'`. The corresponding Ember Data `type` values that would need normalization are `site_customization` and `embeddable_host`, each of which has only a single underscore—so `type.replace('_', '-')` is sufficient for all admin models shown/introduced here. The proposed issue about “multi-underscore admin model names” is speculative and not demonstrated by any model names in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs for embeddable_hosts and embedding only assert superclass identity; create/update/destroy, param handling, nil-record behavior, and staff authorization are untested

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the only controller specs added are `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`, and each contains a single example that merely checks `Admin::<Controller> < Admin::AdminController`. Meanwhile, the controllers introduce nontrivial behavior (e.g., `EmbeddableHostsController#create/update/destroy` and `save_host` param usage via `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`/`[:category_id]`, plus `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`; and `EmbeddingController#show/#update` plus `before_filter ... :fetch_embedding`). None of those behaviors (CRUD responses, parameter handling, authorization, or nil-record cases like `EmbeddableHost.where(...).first` returning nil) are exercised by the new specs. Thus the finding accurately identifies a verifiable gap present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1402 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' is a vacuous test — it no longer exercises host logic and passes only because has_topic_embed? is false

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing any dependence on embeddable-host configuration. In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` the `describe "expandable_first_post?"` section is being edited (diff shows the start of this block) but no corresponding adjustment is shown to ensure `has_topic_embed?` is true when asserting behavior about “embeddable_host(s) blank”. If the test case at/around line 1402 asserts “false if embeddable_host is blank” without setting up a topic embed, it will now be trivially false because `has_topic_embed?` is false, making the test vacuous and no longer exercising host logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:38 sets the category after save from client-side Discourse.Category.findById instead of the server response, showing the wrong category when the server coerced a blank category to uncategorized

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` the `save()` action sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and allows saving even when `categoryId` is blank/null (the `cantSave` computed only checks `buffered.host`). On the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` explicitly coerces a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. However, after `host.save(props)` resolves, the client unconditionally does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))` using the *pre-save* (possibly blank) `categoryId`, not the server-returned `category_id`. If `categoryId` was blank and the server coerced it, this will set `host.category` to `undefined` even though the persisted record now points at uncategorized, so the UI can show the wrong/missing category until a reload.
